newsitem.title: USA: Sabre Group down on soft Nov. air bookings.
newsitem.headline: Sabre Group down on soft Nov. air bookings.

text.p: Sabre Group Holdings Inc's stock dropped Thursday as the market overreacted to soft November bookings for air travel, industry sources said.
Its stock slipped 1-1/2 to 27 by midday trade.
Sabre, the reservation and information systems company spun off by AMR Corp in October, depends on reservations made by travel agents for more than half its $1.5 billion in annual revenues.
While October booking were in line with industry expectations, November bookings were slightly lower, industry sources said.
Air traffic volume remains strong industry-wide, but bookings often fluctuate from month to month based on when air reservations are actually sold.
"The market is overreacting. One soft month will not hurt its (Sabre's) quarter," an industry source said.
November bookings were about two percent below industry expectations, analysts said.
"This is within the normal variation of airline bookings. But December seems to be coming in strong," said Bill Rabin, an analyst with J.P. Morgan Securities.
Rabin said the soft November bookings would not hurt Sabre's earnings. Rabin still expects the company to earn $0.16 a share for the fourth quarter and $1.42 for the year ending December 31.
Analysts' consensus estimates for Sabre are $0.17 a share for the quarter and $1.43 for the year, according for First Call.
